title: Anyone here built their own trading bot? How’s it performing right now?
author: Horror_Office_5737
selftext:
I’ve been building my own bot and I’ve currently got it running in paper trading mode. Rather than rushing it into live trading, I’m planning to let it run for the next 30 days and collect as much data as possible on where it performs well and where it falls apart, then tune the strategy from there.  
For anyone who has actually built and run their own bot  how has yours performed in practice?  
What’s the biggest thing you learned that you wish you’d known before going live? And is there anything specific you’d recommend tracking during the paper-trading phase?  
Would be interested to hear from people who actually built their own rather than using a premade bot.

comments.author: veritas7411
comments.body: I created one in March/April and tried every idea under the sun, had it read the news, spend a bunch of money on API calls, had it try options, you name it. I learned a lot, but essentially built a losing-paper-money machine.  Around July, I rebuilt a v2, and had it be fairly disciplined in what strategy it uses, which didn't include a heavy reliance on LLMs. It trades 3 strategies (crypto-mean-reversion , ETF momentum, and PEAD-8k, the last of which is where I have LLMs read 8k filings and determine if its a good idea to enter a PEAD 5-day hold on a stock).   Since going live mid-July, it's up about 8.5%, some of which is each strategy's beta, but hard to complain giving how its outperformed the market.

replies.author: Horror_Office_5737
replies.body: I see. I’m kind of fortunate with API keys though, I already built a crypto platform so I’m not really out of pocket paying for them, I guess this is just a side project that I would use for my own personal benefit once I feel it’s sitting in a good position. Always said I’d never build one but that changed, fast.

replies.body: I learned a TON building my trading bot, both across trading/algo-trading, but also LLM usage and measurement as well as coding stack... comments.author: mit74
comments.body: Yes I built one by hand a few years ago and invested a lot of time learning strategies. Returns are pretty good of around 5-6% of leverage per month. I rebuilt v2 using AI which has a ton of features and great frontend but is not profitable yet on the same strategies (early days though). Little things add up like bugs, speed of apis, downtime, connection recovery etc. but its early days yet. One thing I'd say though it's a lot of work to make profitable. comments.author: Imaginary_Local9480
comments.body:
I had one built and launched around Feb 2026. Excitement was through the roof. Around April cranked it up for full capital. For next 2.5 months it printed like 1.5% of total capital everyday and ofcourse my human mind thought "this is it, I am set" hahaha. Then it got stuck in few positions and clogged. Printer stopped. Didn't loose money though. Basically it was just riding the bull wave.
It is still live and basically does 0.2-0.4% of capital in a week now. Then couple of months back made another one based on equity microstructure, more like scalper. Its doing paper trading. Interestingly it wins quite fast and early but some days are just too bad and it gives back everything. If I could just block or filter those days then its something which can sustain. Still trying to figure out regime for that. No success so far.

comments.author: Alphanet_dogwalker
comments.body:
Keep one version unchanged for the whole 30 days. If you start tweaking halfway through, run the new version separately. Otherwise you finish the month with results from several different bots and no clean comparison.  
For tracking, give each signal an ID and follow it through sizing, risk checks, orders and fills. Just looking at winning/losing trades makes it hard to tell whether the signal was wrong or the bot handled it badly.

Also, 30 days might tell you quite a lot about bugs and very little about profitability. Depends how often it trades and whether those trades are mostly the same bet. Paper fills are another thing you'll still need to check.
